title: Android, Android TV, and Fire TV: Screen and controls
lead: Start with the Android mobile screen, then try source and player settings, code and SDK operations. The final section explains Android TV and Fire TV remote input.

items.label: Implementation guide: PlayerConfig, source settings, UI customization and FAQ

blocks.text: Preparation and build

Use Java 17 and the required Android SDK packages, then build and launch apps/android. The Android app README covers the requirements and Android Studio or command-line builds. Use Local setup and licenses for shared license configuration.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: The app follows the system or per-app language preference. This guide shows the English app. SDK identifiers, code and returned data retain their original spelling. Standard Player controls also depend on SDK and system language settings.
Android mobile screen and basic controls

The mobile screen below shows the video preview, source and theme selectors, and Settings, APIs, Code and More tabs. Tap a tab to open its workspace without scrolling through other panels. Settings edits configuration, APIs provides commands, state and events, Code shows applied values, and More contains playback helpers and diagnostics. The workspace is shared with the TV app.

blocks.caption: Android mobile, with Source selected in Settings. Choose a field from Setting to open its editor. Reset draft and Apply source stay fixed at the bottom. Android 16 emulator.

items: Select VOD HLS or VOD DASH under Source and start playback. Check that the picture and position advance.
Open Settings → Configuration → Source and Setting → Title. Keep the URL, enter Player Lab VOD and Apply source. Check the reload and title.
Choose Player and set Startup buffer, Restart buffer and Forward buffer to 1, 2 and 10 seconds. Apply player, inspect BufferConfig in Code, and start playback if Autoplay is off.
Switch Theme between Default, Sports, Live and Cinema. The Player and source stay in place while the overlaid controls are replaced.
Inspect applied settings in Code. Use APIs → Commands, State and Events to compare an operation with its result.
Play a live preset and wait for a rewind window before using its controls. Live edge returns to the moving edge. More contains additional live controls and diagnostics.

blocks.text: Return to Default after comparing themes. If a custom theme is missing, follow the implementation guide’s shared-UI build and sync steps. Press Play if playback remains paused after returning from the background.
Configuration drafts and applying changes

Choose Source, Player or SDK overrides under Settings → Configuration, then open a Setting. Source and Player have separate drafts. The fixed action area shows unapplied changes and the pending reload or recreation. Validation errors retain the draft and open the affected field.

In Source, enter an HTTP(S) URL and choose DASH, HLS, Smooth or Progressive. Title, poster and start position are optional. To compare a VOD starting position, set Start offset to 5 seconds, choose Start and Apply source.

For live target latency, enter a value on a live source and Apply source. The applied value survives Player recreation. Clear it and reapply to restore the SDK default. See the implementation guide and test results for its meaning and validation scope.
Player contains playback, buffer and automatic-quality settings. Fields show their units and accepted inputs. The implementation guide’s PlayerConfig section lists defaults and constraints.

blocks.caption: The Autoplay field in Player settings. Apply player recreates the player and reloads its source. Other player settings use the same field selector.

items: Apply source reloads the source on the current Player. Invalid input leaves the active source and Player unchanged.
Apply player recreates the Player with the applied source, excluding unapplied Source edits. Playback restarts at the start offset according to Autoplay.
Reset draft restores the selected Source or Player draft to applied values. Fields and tabs retain drafts. A preset replaces custom source fields and options while retaining Player settings.

blocks.text: Long structured inputs scroll within the editor. The preview, tabs, draft status and Reset/Apply actions remain outside it. Selected values and unavailable actions have distinct indicators.

blocks.title: Menus inside the Android player
blocks.text: The menu inside the video is separate from the app’s Settings workspace. Scroll inside the Player menu to reach hidden options.

items: After applying, inspect Kotlin settings in Code → Player, source and UI. Use Wrap lines for long lines and Copy code for the Android clipboard. The button then shows Copied.
Code excludes unapplied drafts and replaces license values with placeholders. Choose SDK overrides in the code selector for separately applied overrides.

blocks.caption: Applied Kotlin configuration in Code. Wrap lines keeps long statements within the view. The export excludes draft edits and replaces the license with YOUR_PLAYER_KEY.

blocks.title: Reset is not Apply
blocks.text: Reset draft neither changes playback nor restores defaults. An active SDK override remains until removed and applied in its editor. On Android, reapplying valid unchanged basic values deliberately repeats the reload or recreation.
Audio language, external subtitles and retries

items: Set Player audio priority to en, de and Apply player, then Source priority to de, en and Apply source. Compare the selected track in the player menu. Clear the source list and reapply to inherit Player priority.

Enter an HTTP(S) WebVTT URL with an optional label and language such as en-US. Apply source, then select it in the Default UI subtitle menu. To remove it, clear its URL and metadata and reapply, or select a source preset.
Enter HTTP retry delays in seconds, such as 0, 0.25, 2, and Apply player. Blank restores SDK defaults; none disables retries. Compare failed requests on a source you control.

blocks.text: Additional SDK settings

items: Choose Settings → Configuration → SDK overrides. Select a Feature, then use SDK setting to open one property. Search in the selector or browse its category; the editor appears without passing every matching field. Read the SDK name, type, accepted values and units.

Enter a value and choose Stage override. Check the staged changes, then Apply SDK. Staging alone does not affect playback; an applied override takes precedence over the basic settings. For scripts and lists with presets, Preset values inserts an example into the editable field; you can change it before staging.

Choose Code → SDK overrides and refresh the matching API State. Remove followed by Apply restores the basic value or SDK default. Reset draft discards staged edits and restores the applied overrides; it does not remove an active override.

For a callback such as LabelingConfig.videoQualityLabeler, read input and the required result, stage a body and Apply. Trigger the matching SDK path, then use More → Diagnostics to refresh callback outcomes and read calls, fallback and the last fallback reason.

rows: Open the … editor and edit Item/Property. Closing retains the draft. Stage the whole list, then Apply SDK.
Read input and return-type details, stage the body and apply. Trigger its SDK path and inspect call counts in Diagnostics.
Save in More → Startup and integrations, fully close and reopen the app. Compare current and saved next-launch values.

blocks.caption: An applied video-quality label callback. The staged body and active override are visible; the disabled Apply button indicates no pending change.

blocks.text: SDK operations, state and events
APIs separates Commands, State and Events. Select the target before running; search filters candidates. Inspect the call result, state at the last refresh and event history for this app session.

items: Open Commands, search Player.seek, enter 5 for time and Run API. Read any argument or source-state error.

blocks.caption: Commands with Player.seek() and its time argument selected. Run API stays at the bottom. Call result and observed SDK playback state are displayed separately.

items: Choose State, search Player.currentTime and Refresh SDK state. Read the value after seek completion; during playback it continues advancing. Refresh again after another command.

blocks.caption: The selected Player.currentTime value at the last refresh. The value is separate from command submission and remains unchanged until Refresh SDK state is pressed.

items: Choose Events and enable Record SDK events. Clear event counts before the next trial, perform Play/Pause or a supported seek, and inspect occurrence counts and latest SDK timestamps.

Zero means no occurrence has been recorded. PlayerView UI events use a separate prefix; playback belongs to Player and source events to Source. Clear event counts clears the history, not SDK playback state.

blocks.caption: Events with PlayerEvent.Playing selected. The selected event count and the SDK event history since launch are displayed separately.

blocks.text: View commands install fullscreen, Picture-in-Picture and custom Web UI message handlers. Check availability before entering PiP, then inspect its actual view state. Fullscreen returns with Back without discarding editor drafts. Use the matching exit/disable action when finishing a host-feature comparison.

MediaSession connects the current player to Android media controls. Enable the native MediaSession command, inspect the controls, then disable/release it when finished. External-device behavior depends on the host system.

blocks.caption: The native MediaSession command. Enabling it connects the current player to Android media controls; external-device behavior depends on the host system.

blocks.text: Use a compatible source for the VR renderer. Inspect decoded-frame and callback state after starting, then disable the renderer to return to PlayerView. The implementation guide lists content and service requirements.

In More → Analytics, choose collection settings, metadata or runtime actions. Apply Analytics recreates the Player and reloads the source; Reset draft changes only the draft. See Analytics / Observability in the implementation guide for collected-session inspection.
Offline downloads and playback

items: Open More → Offline → Manager. Use sample DASH source or apply a downloadable on-demand source, set Stable content ID and Create manager. Reuse the ID for the same asset.
In Download settings, edit download/segment limits, device/network requirements and offline DRM, then apply. Work may wait until all selected requirements hold.
In Actions, Fetch SDK track options.
In Track selection, set each track to Download, Delete or None. Nothing is selected automatically.
Process selected actions submits the selected set. The SDK may reject actions incompatible with the track state.

blocks.caption: After SDK processing, the audio track shows state=Downloaded, action=null, None selected and progress=100.0%. Choose track actions and use Process selected actions to submit them. Offline playback is checked separately.

items: Inspect Progress and choose Actions → Read offline SDK state, then wait for the manager’s completed state. Only then choose Actions → Play downloaded source and compare video/audio with networking disabled. Track selection or submission is not completion.

In Actions, Suspend downloads and Resume downloads control work in progress. Delete all content for this ID removes its cached content; Release manager keeps the files while releasing the manager. Select a source preset to return to a remote source.

blocks.text: For DRM, inspect media-download completion separately from license download, renew and release. Load saved content with Play downloaded source. The implementation guide covers rights, services and cache requirements.
Android TV and Fire TV screen and remote input
Android TV and Android-based Fire TV use the same app. Use the workspace described above to edit and apply settings and try SDK APIs. Vega OS uses a separate app.

blocks.title: Mobile and TV controls
blocks.text: Default uses touch controls on mobile and remote controls on TV. Sports, Live and Cinema keep their custom themes on TV. See below for TV presentation and remote-input implementation.

items.label: Mobile and TV UI: implementation and remote-input checks

blocks.text: These 1920 × 1080 captures show the normal app on an Android TV API 36 emulator. Default places SDK controls beside the app workspace. D-pad and Select operate the focused item; Back within the SDK preview closes its menu and returns to Source. Fullscreen and native dialogs use their own Back handling.

blocks.caption: Android TV emulator: VOD playback beside Settings → Player → Autoplay. The draft switch and fixed Reset draft / Apply player actions remain in the safe area. Autoplay is off; playback was started separately.

Android TV emulator: APIs → Commands after api.Player.pause(). The editor is scrolled to the observed state, including isPaused=true. The selected operation and fixed Run target / Run API remain visible.

items: Move between Source, Theme and the workspace tabs with the D-pad. Select opens the focused picker; the radio mark shows the selected value.

In a searchable picker, enter a query and close the on-screen keyboard with Back or Done. Focus moves to the first matching option, or Close when no option matches. Use the D-pad and Select to choose a value; a selection alone does not run an API or apply a draft.
When editing a workspace field, Back closes the keyboard and returns to its selector. Done returns to Source. Unapplied values remain available when returning to the editor.
In the SDK preview, test Play/Pause, the timeline and settings. Back returns to Source after closing the SDK menu. Dedicated media keys use the current MediaSession when active.
